about: The flagship line from El Titan de Bronze, a small family-run factory on Calle Ocho in Miami's Little Havana. This version was reblended in 2024 with an Ecuadorian habano wrapper over all-Nicaraguan binder and filler.
notes: This is the 2024 Redemption first sold through General Cigar; the factory took distribution back in August 2026. The maker calls the wrapper Sun Grown Habano without an origin; halfwheel gives Ecuador. The older Redemption Sun Grown and Maduro are separate blends.

about: The maduro version of El Titan de Bronze's Redemption, rolled at the family's factory in Miami's Little Havana. It pairs a Mexican San Andrés wrapper with Dominican and Nicaraguan filler.
notes: A different blend from the 2024 Redemption, which has all-Nicaraguan binder and filler.
verifyNotes: Blend, strength and sizes match the maker's page. Trimmed notes to drop the research remark.

about: A sun grown Ecuadorian habano blend in El Titan de Bronze's Redemption family, rolled in Miami's Little Havana. It uses Dominican and Nicaraguan filler and smokes at medium.
notes: Not the same cigar as the 2024 Redemption, which has all-Nicaraguan binder and filler and comes in three sizes.
verifyNotes: Blend, strength and sizes match the maker's page. Trimmed notes to drop the research remark.

about: The first El Titan de Bronze cigar made outside the United States, rolled at NACSA in Nicaragua rather than at the Miami factory. It has a broadleaf wrapper over a Mexican binder and Nicaraguan filler and is priced well below the Miami-made lines.
notes: Not made in Miami: it is rolled at NACSA in Nicaragua. The maker's page also calls it Redemption Nicaragua. No source states where the broadleaf wrapper is grown.

about: The mild Connecticut-wrapped cigar from El Titan de Bronze, rolled at the family's factory in Miami's Little Havana. The maker pitches it as a morning or first cigar.

about: A full bodied maduro from El Titan de Bronze, rolled in Miami's Little Havana with a dark Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper. The maker says it is not meant for beginners.

about: A dark habano-wrapped cigar from El Titan de Bronze in Miami's Little Havana, sold in bundles rather than boxes. The maker says it is bunched entubado style and finished with a triple cap.
notes: The maker does not publish the binder, filler or where the wrapper is grown. It calls the cigar medium bodied but also says it is not a beginner's cigar.

about: A limited cigar marking 30 years of El Titan de Bronze, which the maker dates to 1995. It comes in one 6.5 x 52 size in boxes of 10, with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan and Dominican tobacco.
notes: Limited release in one size, sold in boxes of 10. The maker gives no release date or production number.

about: One of the original blends from Fermin Perez Cigars, a Miami brand founded in 2021 by Cuban-born Fermin Perez Jr. and made in Estelí, Nicaragua. It is the balanced habano in the core lineup.
notes: The maker does not say where the Habano wrapper is grown and publishes no size list; the 6 x 54 Toro is the only size confirmed. Production moved in September 2026 from Perez's own Estelí factory to Tabacalera Familia Disla; he says the blends did not change.

about: One of the original blends from Fermin Perez Cigars, made in Estelí, Nicaragua. It is a Connecticut shade cigar built to be smooth without being flavorless.
notes: The maker's page calls it medium bodied; the Cigar Press review it cites rated it mild in strength and medium in body, and names the wrapper as Ecuadorian. Only the 6 x 54 Toro is confirmed. Production moved in September 2026 from Perez's own Estelí factory to Tabacalera Familia Disla; he says the blends did not change.

about: The maduro in the Fermin Perez core lineup, made in Estelí, Nicaragua with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over an Indonesian binder and Nicaraguan filler.
notes: The maker calls it full flavored; reviewers put it at medium to full. The Toro also comes in a tube. Production moved in September 2026 from Perez's own Estelí factory to Tabacalera Familia Disla; he says the blends did not change.

about: A box pressed habano from Fermin Perez Cigars, made in Estelí, Nicaragua. It uses an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper and a Habano binder over Nicaraguan filler.
notes: The brand also calls this line simply Royal. The maker publishes no sizes or strength rating and does not say where the Habano binder is grown. Production moved in September 2026 from Perez's own Estelí factory to Tabacalera Familia Disla; he says the blends did not change.

about: A sweet-tipped habano from Fermin Perez Cigars, made in Estelí, Nicaragua as a nod to Miami's Little Havana. The filler includes tobacco from Jalapa and the island of Ometepe.
notes: The cap is sweetened, which is worth telling a guest. The maker publishes no sizes or binder and does not say where the wrapper is grown. Production moved in September 2026 from Perez's own Estelí factory to Tabacalera Familia Disla; he says the blends did not change.
